revision-gated layout: the tolerance is stated in exactly one of them.

oneOf.description: Legacy layout, which states its own solved-cache tolerance.

cache.description: Solved-cache fit contract, absent when the record stated none.

oneOf.description: Revision-gated layout, which states the tolerance in its cache form.

CacheFirstCurveForm.description: Cache-first shared-context fields absent from the context-first layout.

revision.description: Positive serializer-revision integer selecting the cache-first layout.

cache.description: Approximation-cache form selected by the shared context enum.

support_bounds.description: Optional U/V bound fields following each ordered support surface.

solved_range.description:
Optional solved-curve interval endpoints; absent endpoints inherit the
solved NURBS domain.

extension.description: Native integer ASM extension following the discontinuity arrays.

orientation.description: Persisted Inventor axis-angle orientation as X, Y, Z, angle.

properties.description: Other camera fields retained by exact source name.

CenterSource.description: Geometry of a whole-sketch pick that yields hole positions.

oneOf.description: Sketch points.
The centres of circles.
The centres of arcs.

CenterlineAt.description: Where an area station lies on a centerline.

oneOf.description:
A fraction of the centerline's length between the first and the last
section.
A distance along the centerline from the first section.

ChainLayout.description: Components placed along a planar path.

path.description: The path, which lies in one plane.

links.description: How the seeds link along the path.

ChainLink.description: One link of a connected chain.

pins.description: Two axes of the seed's own geometry, both on the path.

ChainLinks.description: How the seeds of a chain link along its path.

oneOf.description:
One link per seed, in the order the seeds alternate. Each link's first
pin axis is the previous link's second, both pin axes of every link
lie on the path, and consecutive pin axes are therefore a chord of the
path as long as the link's own pin distance.
A linkage whose meaning is not established.

picks.description: The entities of the seeds it picks.

Chamfer.description: Bevels edges. A chamfer holds one or more sets, each with its own size.

native_options.description:
Source options whose meaning is not established, and the values of
typed facts whose carrier is unread.

source_settings.description: Source options with no design meaning.

ChamferCut.description:
A chamfer cut along the machined edge with a tapered tool, whose tip runs
`width` times the cotangent of the tool's taper, plus `tip_offset`, below
the edge.

tip_offset.description: The further depth of the tool's tip.

oneOf.description: The distances run along the faces.
The distances offset the faces.
A source measure whose meaning is not established.

reference.description:
The reference face. Where it is `None`, the reference side is the face
whose loop traverses the edge in the edge's own direction.

flip.description: Whether the reference side is swapped.

measure.description: Whether the distances run along the faces or offset them.

ChamferSize.description: The size of a chamfer set. A first distance lies on the reference side.

oneOf.description: An equal setback on both faces.
A setback on each face.

first.description: The setback on the reference side.

second.description: The setback on the other side.

oneOf.description:
A setback on the reference side and the angle from the reference
face.

distance.description: The setback on the reference side.

angle.description: The angle from the reference face.

oneOf.description:
The chamfer face's width across the edge and its angle from the
reference face.

width.description: The width of the chamfer face across the edge.

angle.description: The angle from the reference face.

oneOf.description:
The distance from the edge where the two faces meet to the chamfer
face, and the angle from the reference face.

height.description: The distance from the edge to the chamfer face.

angle.description: The angle from the reference face.

oneOf.description:
Cuts one vertex where three edges of one convexity meet by the plane
through the three points at its distances from the vertex along those
edges, each an arc length on its edge, one per edge.

A source form whose meaning is not established. Its values are native
options under the source's own parameter names.

ChannelAddressing.description:
Index table that addresses a tessellation channel payload.

The domain is the wire's tag, so the selector table exists only on the two
domains that address one: vertex-order addressing has no `indices` key to
leave empty and none to refuse.

oneOf.description: Vertex-order addressing with no explicit index table.
One selector per triangle corner.
One selector per triangle.

Choice.description:
A selection among variants: a stock rule, a WCS mode, a height reference,
a coolant mode.

Where the source holds the choice in parameters, `parameters` names every
parameter the variant is read from, and `value` is the decoder's reading
of them together: a cache, absent where one of their values is absent.
Where `parameters` is empty the source holds the choice as a constant, and
`value` is present.

value.description: The variant the parameters map to.

parameters.description:
The parameters the variant is read from. The variant's own fields bind
their own parameters, and this set does not name them.

CircleMode.description: How an implicit sweep builds its circle section.

oneOf.description:
The circle through the three guides' points; `solution` chooses which of
its arcs.
The circle of `radius` through the two guides' points.

The circle centred at the center curve's point through the reference
curve's point, between the two `angles` measured from the direction
`from` names; the whole circle where both are `None`.

from.description:
The direction the angles are measured from. It decides how the
angles are read.

oneOf.description: The circle of `radius` centred at the center curve's point.

The circle through the `passing` guide's point that touches `surface`
tangentially along the `limit` guide.

passing.description: The guide the circle passes through.

limit.description: The guide along which the circle touches the surface.

oneOf.description:
The circle of `radius` through the `passing` guide's point that touches
`surface` tangentially.

passing.description: The guide the circle passes through.

trim.description:
Whether the tangency surface is trimmed by the sweep and assembled
with it, keeping the portion that makes the result tangent.

oneOf.description:
The circle of `radius` that touches `surface` along the `limit` curve,
which lies on it: its centre lies on the surface's normal at the limit
curve's point, at `radius` from it, between the two `angles` measured
from the surface's tangent plane; the whole circle where both are
`None`.
A source circle mode whose meaning is not established.

CircularLayout.description: An angular run about `axis` and an optional radial run outward from it.

axis.description: The axis of the angular run.

radial.description: The run outward from the axis.

orientation.description:
Whether an instance keeps the seed's orientation or turns with the
layout.

CodecId.description: A codec id: one or more lower-case ASCII letters and digits.

CodecName.description: A codec id, `:`, and a name that holds a character that is not white space.

Coedge.description:
One use of an edge by a loop.

Coedges form a loop ring through the owning [`Loop`] coedge order, and a
radial ring around their shared edge through `radial_next`.

radial_next.description: Next coedge around the edge; self-reference denotes a laminar boundary.

sense.description: Direction relative to the edge curve.

pcurves.description: Ordered parameter-space images of this coedge on the face surface.

use_curve.description: Optional coedge-local 3D carrier used instead of the shared edge curve.

native_ref.description: The source record this coedge projects.

CoedgeUseCurve.description: A coedge-local curve and its loop-traversal interval.

parameter_range.description: Interval on the carrier in loop-traversal order.

target.description: The geometry: a body, or the bodies of an occurrence or a definition.

enabled.description: Whether the simulation includes the collider.

native_ref.description: Format-native record supplying this collider.

ColliderShape.description: The shape a collider gives its target's geometry.

oneOf.description: The geometry itself.

tools.description: The other operands, in source order.

tools_after.description: What the source does with the tools.

new_component.description:

DialectId.description:
A registry dialect id, for example `"rhino:archive-80"`.

Canonical form is `<format>:<name>`. The format contains lowercase ASCII
letters and digits. The name also admits dots and hyphens, but a hyphen
cannot be first or last. Outside the owning codec the validated id is an
opaque label.

Serializes and deserializes as the plain string. Read it with
[`DialectId::as_str`] or print it; there is no other access to the raw
string.

DialectLayers.description:
A report's primary format layer and any nested or carried format layers.

Layers are unique by `(format, instance)`. The wire names the primary
explicitly, so the collection carries its complete identity without an
enclosing report's format.

A read rejects a wire whose `extra` repeats a `(format, instance)` key, and
one whose `extra` carries the primary key. The key set on the wire is the
key set of the value, so no layer is silently discarded or overwritten.

DialectMatch.description:
One format layer's identification of one document.

A document carries several format layers: `.sldprt` contains Parasolid;
`.f3d`, `.ipt`, and SAT contain ACIS; NX contains Parasolid and JT. One
match describes one layer.

declared.description:
Version fields the source declared, verbatim, under keys pinned per
codec in the registry.

Declarations are evidence, never a control input: the dialect is what
the bytes obey, not what they declare.

instance.description:
Instance of this format layer inside the containing document.

`None` when the layer occurs once or has no report-local identity. This
is not source-declared evidence and therefore does not belong in
[`Self::declared`].

with the face's classification and the round trip is stable by
construction. `Unspecified` keeps source order when the source did not

requires it, so a classification that states no outer boundary is not a
state. The two partial arms state a face at least one loop of which the
document does not state (§5.6, Unstated children).

with no boundary is a face with no loop, and nx, sat, step and freecad all
produce one.

through [`Self::boundary`], which answers only for a complete face.

A ball of radius r stays tangent to the listed pieces and to the faces
in `against`, inside every listed piece and outside only a piece in

lies inside and ρ + r from one it lies outside (a cylinder's axis, a
torus's centre circle, a fillet's ball-centre curve): a sphere where
all radii are r; a torus about the R piece's axis, tube r, centre
circle R − r, for r, r, R; and for r, R₁, R₂ the sweep of the ball
whose centre stays at R₁ − r and R₂ − r from the two larger pieces'
loci (R₁ = R₂ included), with, where the sweep reaches the face the
pieces roll on, the ball rolling on the larger piece and on that face.

the torus about its axis, tube r and centre circle R + r. With two,
the corner continues the other listed set's round. With one, that set
is wrapped by another feature's round of radius r. For a cylinder
against a plane normal to its axis the sweep is the torus of tube r
and centre circle R + r.
